summary: Closes Seyi's round-3 QA-03 High finding. Kemi (owns api/Biolog.Api/Tenancy/**) fixed the publicly-forgeable/swappable TenantContext her own round-2 host-channel integration had introduced: TenantContext's record constructor is now internal (only TenantContextMiddleware can construct one), validates TenantId is non-empty and ten_-prefixed, and copies Channels into a ReadOnlyCollection over a fresh list so neither a caller-held list mutation nor a downcast can change it after construction. ITenantContextAccessor is now read-only; the concrete TenantContextAccessor exposes the one authoritative write as an internal SetResolved that is set-once and throws the new TenantContextImmutableException (ADR-0002's tenant_context_immutable) on a second call, matching Decision 3's 'no setter, no swap' literally. TenantModule registers the concrete accessor once per scope and resolves the interface to that same instance. Explicit test seam via InternalsVisibleTo (Biolog.UnitTests/Biolog.IntegrationTests) plus a public TenantContextAccessor(TenantContext?) constructor for a fresh, not-yet-shared instance - not the mid-request swap the fix closes. Collateral, mechanical fix: DeviceServiceTests.cs's ~11 object-initializer sites rewritten to the new constructor form. I independently reviewed the diff line-by-line against Seyi's REREVIEW-ROUND3.md required-closure list (read-only accessor; construction/set restricted to the resolver; set-once/no-swap; frozen Channels; malformed-id rejection; tests for forged construction, reassignment, and collection mutation) and confirmed every item is met, then re-ran the full verification suite myself rather than trusting Kemi's own run.
notes: Full verification, run directly (sandbox disabled only for the dotnet/build commands themselves, per this session's established sandbox-loopback finding - see round-2's evidence notes): dotnet build api/Biolog.Api/Biolog.Api.csproj - 0 warnings/errors. dotnet test: Biolog.UnitTests 154/154 (was 152, +2 for the malformed-tenant-id and channel-mutation tests), Biolog.IntegrationTests 49/49, BIO-TEN-002's own feature suite 90/90, BIO-TEN-001's suite 51/51 (unaffected). bash tests/features/bio-ten-002/BIO-TEN-002.test.sh: 37/37. bash scripts/quality.sh (the full repo-wide gate, not just this story's own harness): QUALITY: PASS, 0 failures - includes contract-freeze, traceability (19 implemented stories), module-project-reference-direction, and the tracked-secret scan, all clean. This is the first round where the full quality.sh gate itself was run and passed clean, rather than just this story's own isolated checks.
